explanation:
### How it works

A valid downward path may begin at any node. For each possible start, a DFS counts paths whose running sum reaches the target. Recursively repeat this count with starts in the left and right subtrees, covering all choices without requiring a path to end at a leaf.

### Steps

1. Count matching downward paths starting at the current root.
2. Repeat the start search for both child subtrees.
3. Add all three counts.

### Complexity

- Time: O(nh), worst-case O(n²) for a chain.
- Space: O(h) recursion stack.

### Things to watch for

- A matching path can stop at an internal node.
- Negative values mean searching must continue after a match.
- This is the simpler repeated-DFS approach; it is not the linear prefix-sum variant.
